items.condition: F is a number field with √−1 ∈ F; F̄ an algebraic closure of F
items.detail: asserted: F = F_mod(√−1, E[2·3·…]) contains √−1 by construction (flag h_F_contains_six_torsion)

items.condition: X_F once-punctured E_F with stable reduction; V^bad_mod ≠ ∅, odd, bad multiplicative; F/F_mod Galois of degree prime to l; E[2·3] ⊆ E(F)
items.detail: checked: V^bad_mod ≠ ∅, odd, multiplicative; the bound on [F:F_mod] is prime to l.  asserted: stable reduction, F/F_mod Galois, E[6] ⊆ E(F)

items.condition: l ≥ 5 prime with Im(G_F → GL_2(F_l)) ⊇ SL_2(F_l); K = F(E[l]); l prime to the residue characteristics of V^bad_mod and to the orders ord_v(q_v) on V^bad
items.detail: checked: l prime, l ∤ p_v and l ∤ ord_v(q_v) for every v ∈ V^bad_mod.  asserted: SL_2(F_l) ⊆ image (flag h_image_contains_SL2)

items.condition: C̲_K a hyperbolic orbicurve of type (1, l-tors)± with K-core C_K = C_F ×_F K; it determines X̲_K of type (1, l-tors)
items.detail: asserted: flag h_CK_is_K_core (fails only for the four exceptional j-invariants)

items.condition: V ⊆ V(K) is a section of V(K) ↠ V_mod (one v above each v_mod); at v ∈ V^bad, C̲_v of type (1, Z/lZ)±
items.detail: |V| = |V_mod| by construction of the data (one v per place listed)

items.condition: ε̲ a cusp of C̲_K from a NONZERO element of Q ≅ Z/lZ; at v ∈ V^bad the cusp of the canonical generator ±1

steps.label: (0) |log q| = log q / 2l: log-volume of the q-pilot at (1,0), i.e. −|log q|
(1) the Θ-pilot at (0,0): naive log-volume −avg(j²)·|log q|
(2) the Θ×μ_LGP-link (0,0)→(1,0) identifies the Θ-pilot with the q-pilot (value groups), units up to Ism
(3) multiradial representation of the Θ-pilot in terms of the mono-analytic data of (1,0): Ind1 count
(4) holomorphic hull, leading terms only: ((l+5)/4)·log d^K (an estimate, not a bound)
(5) leading terms with the theta shift: ((l+5)/4)·log d^K − ((l+1)/24)·log q (not a bound)
(6) −|log Θ| ≤ B: the bound of the proof of Thm 1.10 with every term, summed over v_Q
(7) Cor 3.12 (an input, not re-proved here) gives B ≥ −|log q|, i.e. C_Θ ≥ −1 for C_Θ = B/|log q|

gaps.title: The local fields K_v are known only through bounds
gaps.paper: K = F(E[l]) and, for each v ∈ V, the local field K_v with its ramification index e_v, residue degree f_v, different exponent d_v and p-power roots of unity μ_{p^m}; they enter log(O×_{K_v}), the log-shell I_v and every log-volume.
gaps.code: At a place with p ∤ 30l (F_mod = Q, F = F_mod(√−1, E[2·3·5])) iut_local_field_K writes K_v down: at a Tate-curve place K_v = Q_p(ζ_60l, q_v^{1/30l}) up to an unramified quadratic twist, so e = 30l/gcd(30l, ord q_v), d = 1 − 1/e, m = 0 unless (p − 1) | e, and f from the order of the unit of q_v (JSON data); at a good place e = 1. At p | 30l, where K_v is wildly ramified, and for any other F, e_K and m_K are still the lower bounds forced by q_v^{1/2l} ∈ K_v and by √−1, μ_3, μ_5, μ_l ⊆ K, and f_K = 1. [F:Q] and [K:Q] are upper bounds.
gaps.plan: Partly done: the tame places are exact (each printed value says = or ≥). Left: the wild places p | 30l, which need the Néron model at p (ordinary or supersingular reduction, and for p = l the image of inertia in GL_2(F_l)); the residue degree at good places, which needs the order of Frobenius on E[60l]; and whether the reduction at a Tate-curve place is split, which decides a factor 2 in f when f is odd.

gaps.title: Initial Θ-data is generated only for Frey curves over Q
gaps.paper: Initial Θ-data for any elliptic curve over a number field F with F_mod = Q(j_E), in particular the points of the λ-line of degree ≤ d of Cor 2.2.
gaps.code: `--abc` builds the Frey curve of an abc triple with F_mod = Q; `--theta-json` reads four worked files (also F_mod = Q); `--random` with an odd seed invents a number field by its degree only.
gaps.plan: Open. Needs a number-field layer (minimal polynomial of j, places of F_mod with e, f). The JSON schema already has Fmod.degree and per-place data, so the reader is the place to extend.

gaps.title: l could not be chosen the way the proof chooses it
gaps.paper: A prime l with h^{1/2} ≤ l ≤ 10δ·h^{1/2}·log(2δh), dividing no local height ord_v(q_v), and with ord_v(q_v) < h^{1/2} if l = p_v.
gaps.code: Was: l always given by hand. Now `--l auto` picks the smallest such prime ≥ 7 within IUT_MAX_L (iut_choose_l).
gaps.plan: Done in this change.

gaps.title: A bad place over l was forced into V^bad_mod and the data rejected
gaps.paper: V^bad_mod is a chosen nonempty set of odd bad places prime to l; E may be bad at places of V^good, and Thm 1.10 asks for good reduction only away from 2l.
gaps.code: Was: every odd bad multiplicative place was put in V^bad_mod, so abc(1,2400,2401) with l = 7 failed with an error. Now a bad place over l stays in V^good with a note, and log q, the theta values and f^F leave it out.
gaps.plan: Done in this change.

gaps.title: Five hypotheses of Def 3.1 and one of Thm 1.10 are flags
gaps.paper: √−1 ∈ F; F/F_mod Galois; E[2·3] ⊆ E(F); stable reduction; Im(G_F → GL_2(F_l)) ⊇ SL_2(F_l); C_K a K-core; and for Thm 1.10, F = F_mod(√−1, E[2·3·5]).
gaps.code: Each is a boolean the generator sets to true, or the JSON file records with its proof. The C code does not check any of them.
gaps.where: iut_core.c: iut_validate_data; iut_i.c: iut_def_three_one_check; iut_ops_iv.c: iut_thm110_compute, iut_gap_serre_SL2
gaps.plan: Prepared: iut_gap_serre_SL2 is the placeholder for Serre's criterion (three Frobenius elements), which scripts/infographic/initialtheta-data.js already runs for the four examples; port it to C. K-core: test j ∉ {the four exceptional j-invariants} and no CM. Stable reduction: Raynaud's criterion from E[3], E[5] ⊆ E(F).

gaps.title: The clauses of Def 3.1 were lettered differently from the paper
gaps.paper: (a) √−1 ∈ F; (b) X_F, stable reduction, V^bad_mod, F/F_mod, E[2·3]; (c) l, SL_2, K, l prime to V^bad_mod and ord q; (d) C̲_K, K-core; (e) V a section; (f) ε̲.
gaps.code: Was: the checker put SL_2 and the K-core under (b), the section V under (d) and V^bad_mod under (e), and the validator cited (a) and (e) for conditions of (b). Now both follow the paper, and a clause that is part computed and part asserted says which part is which.
gaps.plan: Done in this change.

gaps.title: A failed clause (c) did not count as a problem
gaps.paper: l is prime to the orders of the q-parameters at V^bad.
gaps.code: Was: l | ord_v(q_v) was a warning in the validator, so `iut pipeline --abc 1 2187 2188 --l 7` printed ✗ at (c) and still ended with 0 problems. Now it is an error and the pipeline counts it.
gaps.plan: Done in this change.

gaps.title: Hodge theaters are records of labels and copy numbers
gaps.paper: Categories: tempered Frobenioids F̲_v, their base categories D_v = B^temp(Π_v)^0, global Frobenioids F^⊛_mod, poly-isomorphisms as sets of isomorphisms, bridges as poly-morphisms of capsules.
gaps.code: A prime-strip is, per v, a tuple of copy numbers (Π_v, G_v, O×) and a list of valuations; a bridge is a flag; a poly-isomorphism is a flag `full_poly_isomorphism` and, in iut_i.c, a count.
gaps.plan: Open, and by design of the data model (docs/DATA_MODEL.md §8). A first real step: represent Π_v at v ∈ V^bad by generators of the tempered fundamental group of the Tate curve and G_v by its (p, e, f) invariants, so that an isomorphism of prime-strips is an actual map.

gaps.title: No element of F_mod^× or κ-coric function is ever written down
gaps.paper: The monoid M^⊛_mod = F_mod^×, the κ-coric rational functions on C_K and their values at the strictly critical points, which give the NF-bridge its content.
gaps.code: Pseudo-monoids are described by name and by Kummer-ready/Kummer-blind flags; the κ-coric check takes a caller-supplied description of a function.
gaps.plan: Open. For F_mod = Q a rational-function type with exact coefficients would do; the global Kummer theory of Prop 3.10 then becomes a statement about real elements.

gaps.title: Theta values are orders and units of q^{j²}, not values of the theta function
gaps.paper: The étale theta function Θ̲_v evaluated at the l-torsion points labelled j gives q̲_v^{j²} = (q_v^{1/2l})^{j²} up to μ_2l, an element of K_v.
gaps.code: The order j²·ord(q_v)/2l is exact, and the unit of q_v^{j²} is computed mod p^8 from the Tate parameter. The 2l-th root q̲_v and the theta series itself are not computed.
gaps.where: iut_pipeline.c: stage 3; iut_input.c: iut_tate_unit_pow; iut_ops_iv.c: iut_gap_theta_value
gaps.plan: Prepared: iut_gap_theta_value is the placeholder. Extracting the 2l-th root needs K_v (gap LocalFieldsOfK); once K_v = F_v(ζ_l, q^{1/l}) is represented, q̲ is a uniformizer power times a unit by Hensel, and the series Σ (−1)^n q^{(n²+n)/2}(U^{2n+1}) can be summed to the same p-adic precision.

gaps.title: The log-shell I_v is given by an inner radius and a model log-volume
gaps.paper: I_v = (p*_v)^{−1}·log(O×_{K_v}) ⊆ K_v, a specific compact Z_p-module, with μ_log(I_v) = log p* − (1/e + m/(ef)) log p; at an archimedean v, the closed disc of radius π.
gaps.code: The radius printed is that of the largest p^λ·O_v the series argument puts inside I_v. Where K_v is written down (p ∤ 30l, see LocalFieldsOfK) μ_log(I_v) = (1 − 1/e)·log p is exact and marked so; at p | 30l it uses the lower bounds for e and m and is marked a model. The archimedean log-volume is set to 0.
gaps.where: iut_lattice.c: iut_apply_log_link; iut_ops_iii.c: iut_log_shell_make; iut_core.c: iut_log_shell_volume
gaps.plan: The wild places follow LocalFieldsOfK. The archimedean term log π per factor is carried in the hull bound (Step (vii)) and should be shown on the shell as well.

gaps.title: The log-link relabels copies; no element goes through a logarithm
gaps.paper: log_v: O×_{†v} → †K_v, whose image becomes the additive module of the next copy ‡; the log-Kummer correspondence follows elements up the column and is only upper semi-compatible.
gaps.code: The link copies Π_v and G_v, gives the units a new copy number and attaches the log-shells. Upper semi-compatibility is a table of three cases.
gaps.plan: Open. With p-adic units to precision p^8 (already used for the Tate unit) the p-adic logarithm of a unit is a few lines; the first use would be to show log(q-unit) inside I_v at each v ∈ V^bad.

gaps.title: The upper bound for −|log Θ| was the two leading terms only
gaps.paper: For each v_Q the procession-normalized bound of Step (v) (distinguished), (vi) (unramified: 0) or (vii) (archimedean: ((l+5)/4) log π), summed over v_Q.
gaps.code: Was: ((l+5)/4)·log d^K − ((l+1)/24)·log q with an estimated log d^K, called an upper bound and used for the verdict. Now iut_hull_bound_compute follows Steps (v)–(vii) place by place with every term, checks that the result is below the C_Θ of the statement, and the verdict rests on it.
gaps.plan: Done in this change. What remains is in the two entries below.

gaps.title: Cor 3.12 is used, not verified
gaps.paper: −|log Θ| ≥ −|log q|: the hull of all possible images of the Θ-pilot, in the multiradial representation and subject to (Ind1)–(Ind3), contains a region of the log-volume of the q-pilot.
gaps.code: The toolkit computes an upper bound B for −|log Θ| and reports whether the consequence B ≥ −|log q| is consistent with the data. It cannot test the inequality itself, and it used to print it with a ✓ as if it had.
gaps.where: iut_lattice.c: iut_multiradial_build; iut_ops_iii.c: iut_cor312_steps; iut_pipeline.c: stage 5
gaps.plan: The wording is fixed in this change. The statement itself is disputed in the literature (Scholze–Stix 2018; the 2026 Lean work), and no computation here bears on that.

gaps.title: (Ind1)–(Ind3) are counted and named, their effect on a region is not computed
gaps.paper: (Ind1) automorphisms of the procession of D⊢-prime-strips, (Ind2) Ism acting on each direct summand of each tensor packet, (Ind3) upper semi-compatibility; the hull is that of the union of the images under all of them.
gaps.code: (Ind1) is the number Π(j+1)!, (Ind2) the number of direct summands, (Ind3) a flag. The union and its hull are replaced by the container of Prop 1.2 (ii) / 1.4 (iii) as in the proof.
gaps.plan: Prepared: iut_gap_hull_exact is the placeholder for the exact log-volume. It needs the tensor packets as actual Z_p-lattices; with LocalFieldsOfK closed, a packet at an unramified p is a free Z_p-module with an explicit basis and the action of Ism is a group of matrices.

gaps.title: The support of the different of F_tpd is not in the data model
gaps.paper: V^dst_Q contains every prime under Supp(d^{F_tpd}); each such prime contributes log p + (l+5)·l*_mod to the bound.
gaps.code: Only the total log d^{F_tpd} is stored. When it is not 0 the hull bound adds ((l+5)/4)·log d^{F_tpd} without those per-prime terms and marks itself incomplete. For the Frey curves F_tpd = Q and nothing is missing.
gaps.plan: Open; goes with GeneratorsFreyOnly: store the ramified primes of F_tpd with their exponents next to dmod.

gaps.title: The hypotheses of Thm 1.10 were not looked at, and its f^F counted the wrong places
gaps.paper: E has good reduction at every v ∈ V(F)^good not dividing 2l; F = F_mod(√−1, E[2·3·5]), hence l ≥ 7; f^F has the support of the q-divisor, V^bad_mod.
gaps.code: Was: the inequality was evaluated for any data, and log f^{F_tpd} included a bad place over 2 (so `--abc 1 8 9` used log 6 where the theorem has log 3). Now the three hypotheses are reported, the verdict line says when the theorem does not apply, and f^F is summed over V^bad_mod.
gaps.plan: Done in this change.

gaps.title: η_prm, ξ_prm, H_unif, C_K, H_K are not given by the papers
gaps.paper: [IUTchIV] only says that η_prm and ξ_prm ≥ 5 exist, and that H_unif, C_K, H_K exist for a compactly bounded subset; the exceptional set Exc_d is finite but not listed.
gaps.code: η_prm = 5·10^20 is borrowed from [ExpEst] (where it serves a sharper form of the prime number theorem); ξ_prm is used only through ξ_prm ≥ 5; Exc is tested by the two conditions the proof makes explicit; C_K is the constant of Thm 1.10 with e_mod = 1.
gaps.plan: Open. For the 4/3 form of Prop 1.6 a far smaller η_prm is admissible (Rosser–Schoenfeld), which would shrink the constant of Thm 1.10 by many orders of magnitude; it needs a citation checked before it goes in.

gaps.title: The explicit abc inequality of [ExpEst] is not in the toolkit
gaps.ref: [ExpEst] Thm A, Thm B, Cor C
gaps.paper: An explicit ε-version of abc and its consequences (e.g. the Fermat exponent bound), with the modified constants of [ExpEst] §1 and the case p = 2 handled by μ_6-initial Θ-data.
gaps.code: Nothing beyond the constant η_prm. The pipeline ends at [IUTchIV] Thm 1.10 and the conditions of Cor 2.2.
gaps.plan: Prepared: iut_gap_explicit_abc is the placeholder. The estimates of [ExpEst] §5 are elementary once the hull bound exists per place, which it now does.

gaps.title: From compactly bounded subsets to all curves: not modelled
gaps.paper: Cor 2.3 obtains Vojta/abc for all hyperbolic curves from Cor 2.2 through [GenEll] (Belyi maps, compactly bounded subsets, bounded discrepancy classes).
gaps.code: iut_cor23_bound evaluates the slack of one inequality; there is no notion of a compactly bounded subset or of ≈.
gaps.plan: Open. Not needed to run one curve through the theory; needed to state what the run proves.

gaps.title: The cross-check compares four numbers, for JSON data only
gaps.code: log q, |log q|, log f and ht are compared with the values stored in the JSON file. Generated data has no independent check, and nothing else in the pipeline is recomputed a second way.
gaps.plan: Prepared: the hull bound now gives a second check (C_Θ place by place must lie below the C_Θ of the statement), which the pipeline counts. Next: recompute ord_v(q_v) from the j-invariant in C for `--abc` data.

gaps.title: The manual is built from a second implementation in JavaScript
gaps.code: docs/IUT_MANUAL.pdf is produced by scripts/manual, which carries its own JavaScript copy of the data model and of the operations for its diagrams and progressions. The fixes of November 2026 (V^bad_mod, Def 3.1 lettering, e_K and m_K bounds, tame K_v, f^F over V^bad_mod, Thm 1.10 hypotheses, the hull bound, Cor 3.12 as an input) are ported and tested (scripts/manual/lib/test.js; the hull bound agrees with the C value), and the manual now prints `iut pipeline` and `iut gaps` from the C program. It is still a second implementation that the next C change will not reach.
gaps.plan: Open: make the diagrams read `iut … --json` (as the guides and articles do) and delete the port.

gaps.title: The GUI and the TUI did not show the gap list or the hull table
gaps.code: Was: only `iut pipeline` and the web app showed them. Now iut-gui has the hull table on the stage 5 page, the placeholders under every stage and in the object tree; the TUI has a gaps screen (key g) and lists the placeholders of stages 5 and 6 under the multiradial screen, which shows B but not the table prime by prime.
gaps.plan: Done.

gaps.title: The Lean mirror of the data types does not have the new fields
gaps.code: lean/ mirrors the structs of iut.h as of an earlier state: no m_K, no h_F_contains_five_torsion, the old rule for V^bad_mod.
gaps.plan: Open.

gaps.title: The prerequisite papers have no operations layer
gaps.paper: The étale theta function and its rigidities ([EtTh]), mono-anabelian reconstruction ([AbsTopIII]), Frobenioids ([FrdI], [FrdII]), general position ([GenEll]).
gaps.code: Their results appear as named facts and flags (cyclotomic rigidity kinds, reconstruction steps of Cor 1.2, tempered facts); none of their constructions is run.
gaps.plan: Prepared: iut_gap_reconstruct is the placeholder for a reconstruction algorithm run on a concrete profinite/tempered group. The two guides (anabelian_guide.pdf, multiradial_guide.pdf) describe the algorithms step by step and are the specification to code against.
